_source: Generated by scripts/stage/build_stage_reference.py from harvey-ahe-project/analysis/stages-train, harvey-ahe-project/analysis/stages-train-c29, harvey-ahe-project/analysis/stages-train-c30 (training runs only). Per stage: active failures = kinds in >= 2 runs of the latest round; policy = kinds that were common earlier and fell to <= 25% of their peak. Regenerated, never appended.

surfaced_not_opened._why: Run fact for the critic: entities that appeared in the agent's search results but were never opened. Shown only at the stages whose most common errors include 'surfaced-not-opened' in the training catalog; disabled if no stage has it.
show_at_stages: Scan document text with an extraction script
Screen candidate matters by reading documents
Search within a candidate matter's files

List files in the document store.purpose: Get an overview of everything in the document store by listing its files, so later steps know what material exists before searching or reading.
List files in the document store.when_to_use: Use at the start of a task, before reading or searching specific documents, to see the full set of files in the store.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a single whole-store glob matching all files to enumerate the store contents.
Ran a whole-store glob and also a shell find or ls of the store folder as a cross-check, avoiding trying to read the folder as a file.
List files in the document store.expected_activity: Getting an overview of the whole store: listing all files (often silently capped at ~100 files from a few matters), or `ls`/`find … \
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

List matter folders.purpose: To get an unfiltered overview of the matter folders in the store, by listing their names or counting files per folder, so later steps know what exists and how it is organised.
List matter folders.when_to_use: Use at the start of a task, when you need to know which matter folders exist or how large the store is, before narrowing down by keyword or opening specific matters.
examples_from_successful_runs: Counted the matter folders with a shell listing, then printed the first and last 20 names to confirm the scale and naming pattern without flooding the output.
When a glob on the matters directory returned nothing, fell back to a shell directory listing, counted the folders and printed the first and last 30 names.
List matter folders.expected_activity: Listing matter folder names (or counting files per folder) across the store, without keyword filtering
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

Search file contents for request keyword.purpose: Locate the matters and files relevant to the request by searching store contents for its keywords, so later steps know which matters to open.
Search file contents for request keyword.when_to_use: Use right after orienting on the request, typically in parallel with a whole-store glob, whenever keywords, names or phrases from the request can point to relevant matters.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a whole-store glob in parallel with a files-with-matches grep for the client name and request keywords, then used the hit list to choose which matters to open.
Ran separate greps over documents and emails, plus a recursive grep -Ril over the store; when a .docx grep returned nothing, switched to text extraction or file-name searches rather than stopping.
Search file contents for request keyword.expected_activity: Running the grep tool (or bash grep -r) over the store for words from the request; often paired with a whole-store glob in the same parallel call
policy: Do not rely on one content grep: if it returns nothing or only email hits, retry with other wording, drop single-extension globs, search file names and matter folders, and extract text from .docx documents so that every qualifying matter surfaces.
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

Scan document text with an extraction sc.purpose: Run a script that unzips document text across the store (or ranges of matters) and searches it for request terms, to build a complete pool of candidate matters for later reading.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.when_to_use: Use when file names and paths alone cannot show which matters contain the needed content, so the text of documents, emails and spreadsheets must be searched store-wide or by matter ranges.
examples_from_successful_runs: Reran a timed-out store-wide scan as several parallel scripts over matter-number ranges, each printing per-matter hit counts instead of full snippets.
Searched documents and emails together for the request's key terms and listed the files and matters with hits, then named candidates from that list.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.expected_activity: Writing a Python/shell script that unzips documents and regex-searches their text across the store (or a range of matters); prone to 60 s timeouts and very large outputs
failure_patterns: After a scan that reached every qualifying matter, a follow-up filter on file names, document types, exact phrases or execution flags, or a cap on printed lines, dropped matters, and the candidate set was built only from the filtered or visible output.

The scan itself missed matters because it was prefiltered by file name or file type, timed out, had a range filter that failed, or was read only partially, and the partial output was treated as the whole store without a rerun or a broader search.
Scan hits listed matters that qualified, but the agent read only a hand-picked or number-ranked subset and never opened the rest.
The script printed snippets for common terms across every matter with no output cap, so the output filled the context and no answer could be written.
Scan document text with an extraction sc.passing_runs: Passing runs kept the scan broad (all matters, documents plus emails), split it into parallel range scripts, or printed per-matter hit counts. They also kept the output to a manageable size, so candidates could be named from what the scan returned.

Search file names for request keywords.purpose: Match the request's keywords against file and folder paths across the store to surface every candidate matter or document for later reading.
Search file names for request keywords.when_to_use: Use at the start of a retrieval task, once the request's key terms are identified, to build a candidate set from file and folder names before opening anything.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran find | grep over file paths for request keywords, then a second pass over folder names for document-type words to catch additional matters, and counted hits per matter.
Ran several parallel globs and path searches for request words and related agreement-type terms across the whole store, and listed full contents of top candidate matters alongside.
Search file names for request keywords.expected_activity: Matching request words against file or folder paths
policy: Never rely on a capped or truncated file-name list: if output hits a line cap, rerun uncapped, page further, or narrow the pattern, and also search document text so matters with unhelpful file names are reached.

Keep the broad path-search result as the master candidate list, and do not drop matters when you narrow patterns or filter to previously named matters; reconcile every narrower search against the broad list, including variant document names and prefixed file names.
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

Search file names for a document type.purpose: Use file and folder path searches for document-type or folder-type words as a stand-in for what the request asks about, typically to list per matter the files of a given type and build a candidate set.
Search file names for a document type.when_to_use: When the request refers to matters or facts that are best located through the kinds of documents they leave in the store (agreements, engagement or intake files, dispute papers) rather than through words the request itself uses.
examples_from_successful_runs: Listed all matter folders alongside a store-wide search for engagement and matter-opening file names, then grouped hits per matter and counted matters per prefix to see which had no match.
Ran a broad path pattern of several document-type words (agreements, subscriptions, term sheets) across all paths, grouped results per matter, then extracted text from a sample of the hit files.
Search file names for a document type.expected_activity: Matching file or folder paths across the store against document-type or folder-type words that the request itself does not use (e.g. engagement-letter files, transaction-document or pleadings folders), as a stand-in for what the request asks about; often a per-matter listing of such files
policy: Treat the file-name search as a broad net, not a final filter: do not narrow the candidate set to matters whose file names match a document-type pattern; cross-check against a full matter listing and keep matters whose documents are named differently, and retry a rescan if it times out.
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

List files in candidate matters.purpose: To enumerate the full file contents of the specific matter folders the agent is considering, or to find a folder's true path, so that candidate matters can be inspected before judging relevance.
List files in candidate matters.when_to_use: Use after a search, scan or name hit has surfaced one or more candidate matters, or when a path guess fails, and you need the complete file list of those matters.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran one shell loop listing all files of every candidate matter that the grep or file-name search hit, including newly surfaced ones.
After a file-not-found error, used find or glob to locate the matter's real subfolder, then listed its files.
List files in candidate matters.expected_activity: Listing every file in one or more specific matter folders the agent is considering, or locating a folder's real path
failure_patterns: Matters that surfaced in the agent's own scans, counts, snippets or file-name searches were left out of the set chosen for listing, because the set was hand-picked, capped by line or number cutoffs, or rebuilt from partial output, so qualifying matters were never listed or opened.
List files in candidate matters.passing_runs: Passing runs listed every matter the search or grep had pointed to, often in a single loop, and added a parallel check across all matters' file names rather than screening candidates by name alone.

Read documents picked from the file list.purpose: To open and read documents chosen from the store listing so the agent understands the matters it is looking at, using the listing as a starting point for reading rather than as the full picture of the store.
Read documents picked from the file list.when_to_use: Use when the task needs document content and no keyword-search lead points to specific files, so the choice rests on the file listing, typically the matter at the top or a few matters sampled from it.
examples_from_successful_runs: Read a batch of memos, emails, and engagement letters from the matter at the top of the listing, then followed with engagement letters from several other listed matters to widen coverage.
Sampled the opening lines of engagement letters across different number prefixes to get a quick sense of several matters, accepting that guessed folder paths may fail and moving on.
Read documents picked from the file list.expected_activity: Opening documents chosen from the (partial) store listing with no keyword-search lead behind the choice
policy: Treat a capped or partial listing as a sample, not the whole store: before concluding that something is absent or counting across matters, run a store-wide keyword search or otherwise widen coverage, and never restrict scripts or conclusions to the few matters shown at the top.
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

Screen candidate matters by reading docu.purpose: Open and read the beginnings of documents from several candidate matters to judge which ones actually fit the request and to collect the proof documents needed to cite them.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.when_to_use: Use after searches or scans have surfaced a set of candidate matters and you must decide, by reading their key documents, which fit and what each one's role is.
examples_from_successful_runs: Read the opening of executed agreements from five to ten matters surfaced by the scan, one per matter, to compare defined terms and amounts.
Opened closing memos and status reports from three candidates picked by the most specific grep hits, retrying when a guessed path did not exist.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.expected_activity: Reading the opening part of documents (engagement letters, memos, filings) from several candidate matters to judge whether each fits the request
policy: Tally every matter and number series shown in complete listings before choosing what to verify, and check each series' client so none is omitted from the ranking.
failure_patterns: Matters that surfaced in the agent's own searches, scans or candidate lists were left out of the reading shortlist, never opened, and so dropped from or misclassified in the answer from snippets alone.

A matter's needed proof document (executed agreement, closing or covenant memo, complaint or motion, spreadsheet) appeared in a listing, but the agent opened or cited other documents of that matter or a sibling matter instead.
A matter's proof document never appeared in any search or listing because the agent never listed that matter's folder, so it read peripheral papers and cited no proof record.
Screen candidate matters by reading docu.passing_runs: Passing runs picked reads directly from the scan hits and listings, covering every matter with specific hits, and opened the key document (executed agreement, closing memo, complaint, status report) in each rather than peripheral papers.

Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.purpose: To read the key sections and supporting documents of the matter(s) the agent has settled on in enough depth to extract the concrete details needed for the answer.
Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.when_to_use: Use once candidate matters have been narrowed to one or a few and you need to open their governing, closing, outcome and supporting documents to confirm and extract details.
examples_from_successful_runs: Opened the executed agreement, then its closing, side-letter and subscription documents, reading long files section by section or at offsets so nothing was skipped.
Listed the matter's folder when a guessed path failed, then opened every outcome memo, certificate, order and engagement letter it found rather than leaving listed documents unread.
Read a chosen matter's documents in dept.expected_activity: Reading further sections/documents of the matter(s) the agent has settled on, to extract details and supporting documents
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

Search within a candidate matter's files.purpose: Run targeted grep or snippet extraction inside a single candidate matter folder or document to confirm whether it contains the facts, terms, or names the request needs.
Search within a candidate matter's files.when_to_use: Use after candidate matters have been surfaced and you need to verify or pull specific clauses, dates, names, or phrases from their files before deciding which to read in depth.
examples_from_successful_runs: Ran a capped snippet script over the executed agreements of a few named candidates to pull governing-law and consideration clauses, then reran on the single best match.
When a name scan over a matter's files printed nothing, checked that the folders existed and reran with a more robust extraction and per-matter hit counts.
Search within a candidate matter's files.expected_activity: Grep or snippet extraction restricted to one matter folder or one document
policy: Whenever a file for a candidate matter appears in a listing or search, include its executed or primary document in the next extraction or read rather than substituting secondary correspondence.
failure_patterns: Snippet scripts were run over many matters or whole-document text with greedy patterns, wide context windows, and no output cap, so the oversized output filled the context and the run ended with no answer written.

Relevant files and matters that had already surfaced in path searches or scans were left out of the hand-picked list for later snippet scripts and reads, so they were never opened and their evidence was missed.
Search within a candidate matter's files.passing_runs: Passing runs capped output and scoped scripts to a small named set of candidate matters or to specific agreements, printing per-matter hit counts and sanity checks. They confirmed folder paths when a script printed nothing, and widened to other matters only in controlled batches.

Calculate figures for the answer.purpose: Compute the derived values the deliverable needs (counts, distributions, day counts, averages, rates) with a short script that works only from figures already read, without touching the document store.
Calculate figures for the answer.when_to_use: Use after the source data (such as a saved folder list or scan file) has been read and the answer needs counts or per-group figures computed from it.
examples_from_successful_runs: Counted items per group from the saved folder list file, covering all groups rather than only the leading few, and reported the full distribution.
Computed coverage and per-group counts from the saved scan file in one short script, with a single memo read to support the figures, after opening the stage properly before making calls.
Calculate figures for the answer.expected_activity: A short script that computes values for the deliverable (day counts, averages, rates) from figures already read; it does not touch the document store
failure_patterns: No recurring failures (seen in two or more runs) were recorded at this stage in the latest training round.

Write the response.purpose: Write the final deliverable file that answers the request, listing the qualifying matters with accurate facts, identifiers and supporting documents, plus any excluded candidates with reasons.
Write the response.when_to_use: Use after the search and reading are done, once the matters have been checked against the request's scope and the answer file is ready to be written or overwritten.
examples_from_successful_runs: Writes the response with two or more qualifying matters, cites the executed agreement and key documents for each, and adds a separate list of excluded candidates with reasons.
Writes that no matter meets every part of the request and explains why each near candidate falls short.
policy: Always state the matter number and name the specific documents (such as closing memos or issues memos) read for each included matter.
State explicitly that each qualifying matter closed or was executed, and give the firm-wide conclusion the question asks for instead of declining to generalize.
Open the documents of any matter surfaced in a scan before writing, and compare candidates rather than skipping them.
failure_patterns: The answer lists as qualifying matters that fall outside the requested scope (other practice groups or books, drafts, term sheets, unexecuted, withdrawn or proposed deals, adjacent precedents, and deals whose documents show a different purpose or structure), inflating the set and the counts.

The answer excludes matters that qualify, judging them from snippets, file names, emails or pre-closing papers without opening their executed or closing documents, or by reading the criteria too narrowly (formation, project financing, acceleration, recommendation memos), or omits a listed matter with no stated reason.

The answer misstates facts of included matters: wrong buckets or classifications, wrong amounts or dates, closed deals described as planned, settlements recorded as paid rather than recovered, or descriptions swapped between matters because parallel read results were paired with the wrong paths.
The answer omits details the request needs, such as the client and outcome of a review or the subject of a listed but unread dispute.
Write the response.passing_runs: Passing runs named only matters whose documents they had verified, stated exclusions with reasons, and explicitly said when no matter met a strict reading, listing near candidates with why each fell short.

Check or revise the response.purpose: Re-read the written response and verify cited paths and details, making only edits that keep the final answer accurate, correctly scoped and honestly worded.
Check or revise the response.when_to_use: Use after drafting the response and before finalizing: re-read it, confirm every cited file path exists, spot-check a cited detail against its source, and fix wording on scope or completeness.
examples_from_successful_runs: Globs or loops to confirm each cited path exists, corrects a wrong path in the response, and re-reads the response afterward.
Re-reads the top of a source document or greps for a date to confirm a cited detail, then softens an overclaimed completeness statement to match the reviewed scope.
Check or revise the response.expected_activity: Editing the written response, re-reading it, or re-checking a cited path/detail after writing
policy: Do not remove or move qualifying matters out of the counted set during final edits unless their own documents clearly fail the criteria; do not delete rows as duplicates when each has its own executed document.
failure_patterns: During the final edit, items are added to or restored in the qualifying set on weak grounds (a reference to an earlier matter, a different matter number, a reclassification from a wider search, or reinstating items already demoted) even though the item's own documents do not meet the stated criteria.
Check or revise the response.passing_runs: Passing runs limited edits to cited paths and to softening completeness, exclusivity, recency or scope wording, and confirmed details against source files rather than changing which matters were counted.
